title: Salt Length vs. Merkle-Damgard Call Count in Random Oracle Combiners
statement_paraphrase: Does a secure Merkle-Damgard-style random oracle combiner exist with O(lambda)-length, message-independent salts and O(1) calls to the underlying hash functions, or is that combination impossible and what is the true salt-length/call-count trade-off?

evidence.claim: Source paper (Dodis, Goldin, Hall, EUROCRYPT 2025) states this as its main open problem in the Conclusion.
No follow-up work found resolving the salt-length/call-count trade-off; search results only describe the source's own resolution of the prior DFGHP23 conjecture, not this further question.

queries_run: "random oracle combiner" Merkle-Damgard salt length constant blocks 2026
"random oracle combiner" O(lambda) salt sublinear calls Merkle-Damgard open problem solved
"Random Oracle Combiners" "Merkle-Damgard" follow-up citing open problem salt length 2026

G1_barrier.evidence: No barrier language in the source; not identified as implying resolution of a named external open problem.

G4_dual_use.evidence: Idealized-model construction/impossibility question, not a concretely instantiable attack on a deployed system.

P1.justification: Either exhibit a combiner (construction-friendly) or prove impossibility plus a trade-off (lower-bound-style); genuinely two-sided.
P1.construction_side_dual: Search over combiner constructions -- not necessarily salt-and-XOR -- for one achieving O(lambda) salts and O(1) Merkle-Damgard calls.

P2.justification: Base case (unbounded salt, works) is settled; next rung (O(lambda) salt) is well defined but the gap to it is asymptotic, not a narrow few-rung ladder, and no specific proof feature is nameable as surviving the shrink.
P2.restriction_axis: salt length relative to message length

P3.justification: Hard cap applied: removing the |M|-dependence entirely plausibly needs a combiner paradigm the source does not sketch, not just a parameter tweak to its own simulator argument.
P3.candidate_technique: compression-argument simulator recursion (source Theorem 3.1), if it can be extended at all

V1.justification: Precisely quantified via the source's own indifferentiability definition; one genuine ambiguity is whether calls are counted against the letter (invocations of h1*,h2* as named) or their spirit (any equivalent computation), which is nameable but real.
V1.vacuous_reading: A construction that satisfies the letter of 'O(1) calls to h1*, h2*' by restructuring computation to avoid naming those calls while doing equivalent work elsewhere.

V2.justification: Indifferentiability's deliverable is a simulator valid against all distinguishers; like Feistel indifferentiability, there is no finite decision procedure or scalar score for the general existence question, only a hardenable but not exhaustively-checkable predicate.
V2.finite_instantiation: toy Merkle-Damgard compression functions at tiny parameters, but security still requires a simulator argument, not brute-force decidable

V3.justification: EasyCrypt/SSProve support game-hopping generally, but the decomposition for a genuinely new combiner paradigm's simulator is itself the research content.
V3.decomposition_cost: high -- the simulator IS the open question

O1.justification: Explicitly flagged as 'the main open problem' by the source (deliberate, not a passing aside), so no +2; but very recent and low independent attention.

O2.justification: Source and prior art fully open-access; bounded compute profile; but a full novel-paradigm construction plausibly runs long with no clean lemma boundary.

reasons: R4: the call-counting predicate is gameable by restructuring computation, as noted under V1's vacuous reading.

configuration.entry_rung_latex: Does there exist a secure ROC with $|Z_1|,|Z_2|=O(\lambda)$ and $O(1)$ calls to $h_1^*,h_2^*$?
configuration.leading_plan_class: Scout plus Refuter (search for a non-salt-and-XOR combiner or a counting-style impossibility argument), Case Planner to name intermediate salt-length rungs between the source's bound and O(lambda).
configuration.falsifiable_milestone: Either a toy-parameter combiner construction candidate with a plausible (even if not fully proved) simulator sketch achieving sub-linear salt growth, or a concrete counting argument ruling out a wide class of salt-and-XOR variants.
configuration.yield_on_failure: A barrier note on why salt-and-XOR combiners cannot avoid the |M|-dependence, narrowing the search space for future attempts.
